runtime.scope: Recorded-feedback replay through C frame validation, paired conversion scaling, per-channel reference/PI state and packed PWM compares; exact agreement with the independent serial state machine and compiled kernel. Behavioral wake/readback/fresh-channel sequencing wraps the runtime. Hardware arming is an injected healthy input; not a new physical trajectory, cold-rail transient or GPIO/DMA deployment.

feedforward_approximation.method: Linear interpolation uses max abs(tanh second derivative)=4/(3 sqrt(3)); saturation tail is explicit. Rounding reserves eight float32 relative epsilons times the voltage scale.
feedforward_approximation.scope: Feedforward voltage before PWM quantization; not a closed-loop trajectory-equivalence bound

limitations: RP2350-family clock and PWM candidate only; board-level clock tolerance, pin assignment, firmware and processor worst-case execution time are not qualified.
Phase-correct TOP and compare latches follow the datasheet; all PWM slices must be started synchronously. A carrier is assigned to each paired channel readout.
The SPI guard is rounded upward to whole system clocks. Conversion, transfer and compute precede the same carrier latch used by the analog control screen.
The allocated compute duration is a design assumption. The maximum cycle count is a scheduling deadline, not evidence that code meets it.
Shared command transport, fault handling, calibration and Hall sensing need separate timing/resource allocations.

Runs C reference filtering and the PI/feedforward/PWM kernel inside the existing averaged plant. C acquisition-to-PWM runtime is separately checked by recorded-feedback replay; GPIO/DMA deployment and execution time remain unverified.
The same source compiles for Cortex-M33, but only the host binary is executed here. ARM library linkage, runtime and cycle timing are not established.
The bounded interpolation removes the transcendental library call. Kernel, reference filtering, acquisition and PWM writes still need processor cycle-time verification.
No interrupts, DMA contention, flash stalls or processor faults are simulated by this compilation check.
